Police Scotland modernises search operations with Esri GIS

2026-09-24 Industry Press Release (Geo Week News) Police Scotland, Esri, GIS, search operations, missing persons, mobile mapping, Esri Award, Commonwealth Games, public safety
Read the source article

Quick summary

Police Scotland has won an Esri Special Achievement in GIS Award for transforming search operations with mobile mapping apps and interactive dashboards, replacing paper-based processes to find missing people, secure Royal visits, and protect major events like the Glasgow Commonwealth Games.

Key takeaways

  • Police Scotland won an Esri Special Achievement in GIS Award for modernising search operations
  • The Missing Persons Module helps plan and allocate search resources including dog teams, drones, diving units, and mountain rescue
  • Mobile devices give field officers search boundaries and assignments, replacing paper maps and manual notes
  • The system was most recently used at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow in July 2026
  • Training for nearly 300 users has been completed across the 23,000-officer force covering 28,000+ square miles
  • Search and seal operations created for COP26 in 2022 completed up to 75% faster with geospatial tools
  • Virtual models of regularly searched locations like Holyrood House speed up security checks
